room: The visitor is sitting with Vincent on a small hilltop above Saint-Rémy at night. The sky, the stars, the crescent moon, the cypress, the village with its church and the far hills are from his painting The Starry Night, made in June 1889 at the asylum in Saint-Rémy from the view east of his window before sunrise, and from memory. The hilltop itself, its grass, path, bushes and flowers, the rock he sits on, the lantern on its post, the blanket, the clouds and mist round the rim, his sketchbook and the torn page were made for this visit; they are not in the painting. In the visit the visitor turns the lantern down, wakes the stars he names, follows the wind across the sky, and stays until dawn.
pointOut: say which one they mean, for example the cypress, the moon, the village or the lantern

objects.knows: He painted the stars as whirling rings of light, far bigger than they look, each in its own halo, to show how alive the night felt to him.

objects.what: the big bright star just right of the cypress
objects.knows: Often read as the morning star, Venus. He wrote of seeing the countryside from his window before sunrise with nothing but the morning star, which looked very big.
A crescent moon in a blazing orange-yellow halo, top right, as bright as a sun: he painted the night full of light rather than dark.

objects.what: the great swirl across the sky
objects.knows: The swirl through the middle of the sky: the wind, or the night itself, moving. He let the strokes curl and flow so the sky feels alive while the village below sleeps.
The cypress rises in front like a dark flame, joining the earth to the sky. He loved cypresses for their lines and their deep green, and said they were as beautiful as an Egyptian obelisk.

objects.what: the village with its church below
objects.knows: The quiet village with its lit windows and a pointed church spire, calm and small under the moving sky. The spire looks more like a church of his northern homeland than one from Provence.

objects.what: the far hills behind the village
objects.knows: The rolling hills behind the village, the Alpilles, painted with the same rhythm as the sky.

objects.what: the grassy hilltop, its path, bushes and flowers
objects.knows: Made for this visit, so the visitor can sit where the view is. In the painting the near ground is only the cypress and dark slopes.
The rock he sits on for this visit, made for it.
A lantern on an iron post, made for this visit: the visitor turns it down so the stars can come out.

objects.what: the striped blanket on the grass
objects.knows: A striped blanket in the painting's colours that marks where the visitor sits, made for this visit.

objects.what: the clouds and mist round the hill
objects.knows: The clouds and mist round the rim of the hill were made for this visit, so the world seems to fall away.
In this visit it is his sketchbook, open to a sketch of this view. He says the hills in it are right, but the sky is not yet.

objects.what: the torn page he leaves on the rock
objects.knows: A torn page with his sketch, which he leaves for the visitor at dawn.
The stick of charcoal he holds, for sketching the view.
